import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 940

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/940](https://www.erdosproblems.com/940)
- [BaBr94] Baker, R. C. and Brüdern, J., _On sums of two squarefull numbers_. Math. Proc.
  Cambridge Philos. Soc. (1994), 1-5.
- [He88] Heath-Brown, D. R., _Ternary quadratic forms and sums of three square-full numbers_.
  (1988), 137-163.
-/

open Filter

namespace Erdos940

/--
Let $r \ge 3$. Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most $r$ $r$-powerful numbers
has density $0$?
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_940 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3,
      {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry

/--
The set of integers which are the sum of at most two $2$-powerful numbers has density $0$.

Erdős called this 'easy'. Baker and Brüdern [BaBr94] gave the first proof in the literature.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_940.variants.two :
    {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ),
      S.card ≤ 2 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ n = S.sum}.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry

/--
Is it true that the set of integers which are the sum of at most three cubes has density $0$?

The cubes are those of non-negative integers, which is what `Multiset ℕ` gives. This choice
decides the question: over `ℤ` a sum of three cubes is conjectured to represent every integer
that is not $\pm 4 \bmod 9$, which is density $7/9$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_940.variants.three_cubes :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    {n : ℕ | ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ n = (Multiset.map (· ^ 3) S).sum}.HasDensity 0 := by
  sorry


/--
Let $r \ge 3$. It is not known if all large integers are the sum of at most $r$-many
$r$-powerful numbers.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_940.variants.large_integers :
    answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ r ≥ 3, (∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ x = S.sum) := by
  sorry

/--
Heath-Brown [He88] has proved that all large numbers are the sum of at most three
$2$-powerful numbers.

This is the case $r = 2$ of `Erdos1107.erdos_1107`, which asks the same question with $r + 1$
summands, and it is stated there as `Erdos1107.erdos_1107.variants.two`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_940.variants.three_powerful :
    ∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ (S : Multiset ℕ), S.card ≤ 3 ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, (2).Full s) ∧ x = S.sum := by
  sorry

end Erdos940

findings.description: The RHS at line 76 asserts that, for every r ≥ 3, all sufficiently large integers ARE representable using at most r r-powerful numbers. The source's first question asks whether, for every r ≥ 3, infinitely many integers are NOT representable. Writing Rep r n for the representation predicate, the source asks `∀ r ≥ 3, ¬ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, Rep r n`, whereas Lean asks `∀ r ≥ 3, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, Rep r n`. This is not merely an equivalent question with the overall answer reversed: negating Lean's RHS gives `∃ r ≥ 3, ¬ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, Rep r n`, not the source's universal assertion. The fixed-r equivalence between infinitely many exceptions and failure of eventual representability, and this quantifier distinction, were checked in Lean.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/940: “Let r ≥ 3. ... Are there infinitely many integers which are not the sum of at most r many r-powerful numbers?” The original [Er76d], pp. 33–34, formulates this as G_p(r) > r, with G_p(r) the least number of summands sufficient for every sufficiently large integer. Its correction on p. 42 says that G_p(r) > r does not follow from the claimed counting argument and remains open. Original paper: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert negation inside the universal quantifier: `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ r ≥ 3, ¬ (∀ᶠ x in atTop, ∃ S : Multiset ℕ, S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ x = S.sum)`. Equivalently, assert that `{n : ℕ | ¬ (∃ S : Multiset ℕ, S.card ≤ r ∧ (∀ s ∈ S, r.Full s) ∧ n = S.sum)}.Infinite` for every r ≥ 3. Update the docstring to ask about infinitely many unrepresentable integers.

reformulations.difference: The multiset summands range over ℕ, and `Nat.Full r 0` holds, whereas powerful numbers are ordinarily taken to be positive.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Because the bound is “at most r”, every zero summand can be deleted without changing the sum or increasing the cardinality. Conversely, every representation with positive summands is already allowed. The scratch file proves the pointwise representation-predicate ↔ for arbitrary r, summand bound k, and target n after adding `0 < s` to each summand's condition. The same argument applies to the other powerful-number variants. Inclusion of the target 0 through the empty sum does not affect density or eventuality.

reformulations.difference: Lean uses at most three nonnegative cubes; the original paper discusses three positive cubes. The current Erdős webpage already uses “at most three”.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The original paper's discussion of Davenport's positive-cube result confirms that signed integer cubes are not intended. Removing zero bases gives an equivalent at-most-three-positive-cubes representation; this pointwise equivalence was proved in Lean. Compared with exactly three positive cubes, the additional integers are sums of at most two positive cubes, of which there are O(N^(2/3)) below N. Thus the two sets have density zero simultaneously. The final density equivalence with exactly three positive cubes was not formalized in the scratch files.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/940 (statement, remarks, and status; read through the Jina rendering proxy)
https://www.erdosproblems.com/forum/discuss/940 (mathematical discussion, including Tao's squarefull-number argument and the clarification of “NOT all large integers”)
P. Erdős, Problems and results on number theoretic properties of consecutive integers and related questions (1976), pp. 33–34 and correction on p. 42: https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1976-39.pdf
https://www.erdosproblems.com/1107 (the distinct r+1-summand question and its r=2 case)

R. C. Baker and J. Brüdern, On sums of two squarefull numbers, Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society 116 (1994), 1–5: https://doi.org/10.1017/S0305004100072340 (publisher's extract and bibliographic metadata)
review.notes: All five declarations were checked. `Nat.Full` agrees with divisibility by p^r for every prime divisor; `HasDensity` uses real-valued natural-density ratios over finite initial intervals; and `atTop` here is the nontrivial filter on ℕ. Small powerful-number and cube-sum cases were evaluated, and the cross-reference to problem 1107 was verified via a List/Multiset equivalence. All three experiment files under /workspace/review/ compile. The full Baker–Brüdern and Heath-Brown texts were not accessible; their stated solved results were checked against the explicit cited Erdős pages and mathematical remarks. The reviewed file matches the specified commit exactly.

submission.summary: Inserted negation inside `∀ r ≥ 3`, so the statement asks whether infinitely many integers are unrepresentable for each r. Updated the docstring accordingly and left all other declarations and attributes unchanged. The prescribed compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warnings.
